macro: US equity indices are mixed at midday with the S&P 500 flat, Nasdaq up 38 basis points, Russell 2000 up 30 basis points, and the Dow down 43 basis points. Treasuries are pretty flat across the curve, while Brent crude is off fractionally near $100 as UN diplomacy around Iran and the resumption of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline ease some supply fears. Gold, silver, and bitcoin are all modestly lower on the session.
rates_fed: Treasuries are essentially unchanged across the curve with no major rate or Fed catalyst driving action today. The macro focus remains on geopolitical developments in the Middle East rather than monetary policy. No Fed speakers or data releases are moving the needle intraday.
market_outlook: Adam's tone is cautiously neutral with a slight bullish lean into the AI catalyst runway — the market is in a holding pattern as investors await UN developments on Iran and a string of critical AI events over the next week and a half, including Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, OpenAI's DevDay on September 29th, and Micron earnings on September 30th. The key catalyst to watch today is the KBH and WOR earnings after the close.
bull_case: The AI catalyst pipeline is loaded — Meta Connect, OpenAI DevDay, and Micron earnings all hit within 10 days, and Meta's Muse agent is already seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote. Pockets of tech, housing, travel/leisure, and consumer staples are all outperforming, suggesting underlying breadth is reasonably healthy. Geopolitical risk is incrementally easing with Iran signaling openness to Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline coming partially back online, which could reduce energy-driven macro headwinds.
bear_case: Financials are broadly under pressure — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers are all underperforming, which is a notable headwind for the equal-weight index and signals concern about the economic backdrop. Lab testing names are getting hit on larger-than-expected CMS Medicare rate cuts, managed care is weak, and aerospace/defense is selling off, suggesting defensives and rate-sensitive names aren't providing cover. Trump's approval rating hitting a career low of 32% adds political uncertainty, and the SB Energy IPO delay signals cooling sentiment on the data center boom.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by tariff refunds that provided a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind and a non-cash LIFO impact worth another 105 basis points. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, though management noted positive sales linearity in the quarter, which is helping the stock rally.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding the tariff refund tailwind of 11 cents — clean EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged, making this a solid quality beat overall.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% expectation. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% year-over-year but slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate, and management cited a difficult macro landscape.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform — a meaningful distribution win. Investor expectations are growing more bullish into the event, and OpenAI is reportedly considering a competing product, validating the market opportunity.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, giving Muse a major checkout integration ahead of Meta Connect. This contrasts with Amazon's decision to block Muse from its platform, positioning Shopify as a key beneficiary of the agentic commerce wave.

PSKY is spiking after the company obtained a relatively favorable settlement deal from a group of state attorneys general, removing a major legal overhang. The resolution is being viewed as a positive clearing event for the stock.

Quest Diagnostics shares are under pressure after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services, with the reductions coming in larger than the market had anticipated. The rate cuts hit both Quest and Lab Corp simultaneously, creating sector-wide selling pressure in lab testing names.

Lab Corp is selling off alongside Quest Diagnostics following new CMS Medicare lab service payment rates that were larger reductions than the Street expected. This is a direct reimbursement headwind with no near-term offset visible.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the Physical AI and robotics ecosystem at a time of accelerating industry investment.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including 22% weight loss in the study. This is a meaningful clinical readout that reinforces Viking's competitive position in the obesity drug market.

sectors: Financials are broadly weak — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all underperforming, suggesting macro caution. Lab testing is getting hit by CMS Medicare rate cuts larger than expected, dragging managed care down too. Tech is bifurcated — AI-adjacent names like ARM, ASML, GOOGL, META, MU, and ORCL are outperforming while enterprise software and networking names like MSFT, CRM, CSCO, ANET, and PANW are lagging. Housing stocks DHI, LEN, and PHM are outperforming. Auto parts retailers AZO, GPC, and ORLY are rallying on positive sales linearity commentary. Travel and leisure names including airlines and cruise lines are seeing broad strength. Texas Governor Abbott ordering a halt to new data center permitting in the state is a notable headwind for the data center buildout narrative.

That geopolitical relief is keeping a lid on oil prices but also keeping a floor under overall risk sentiment. On the company front, AutoZone is rallying after beating on fiscal fourth quarter earnings, but it is worth noting the beat was low quality — tariff refunds and a non-cash inventory accounting benefit did the heavy lifting, and domestic comps came in at plus 1.6 percent versus the Street at plus 3.1 percent. Management's comment that sales linearity was positive in the quarter is what is keeping the stock bid. MillerKnoll was a clean beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and even stripping out the tariff refund tailwind of 11 cents, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. That is the kind of quality beat the market rewards. On the downside, THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter earnings at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year. Management acknowledged the difficult macro environment. Lab testing names Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are both getting hit after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that came in with larger reductions than the Street had modeled. That is a direct reimbursement cut with no near-term catalyst to offset it. On the AI front, Meta's Muse personal agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote tomorrow night, and Shopify announced it will integrate Muse for agentic checkout on its platform. That is a meaningful distribution win for Meta heading into what is shaping up to be a pivotal week and a half for the AI trade — Meta Connect tomorrow night, OpenAI's developer day on the 29th, and Micron earnings on the 30th. Viking Therapeutics reported 22 percent weight loss in its GLP-1 drug trial, which is a strong clinical result that keeps them competitive in the obesity space. Cognex is acquiring RealSense, the leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly 500 million dollars upfront. Sectorally, financials are broadly weak across banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers. Tech is bifurcated with AI-adjacent names outperforming and enterprise software lagging. Housing, travel, auto parts retailers, and consumer staples are all showing strength. The directional read here is cautiously neutral with the market in a holding pattern ahead of the AI event runway. The bull case is that the catalyst pipeline is loaded and sentiment is building. The bear case is that financial sector weakness and political uncertainty — Trump's approval rating hit a career low of 32 percent in a new poll — could weigh on the broader tape if macro fears resurface. Watch the KBH and WOR earnings after the close tonight, and position for Meta Connect tomorrow night.
